summary: One machine in the workspace, holding the image, and nobody counted its cards. Its agent could not run the vendor tool, so it reports everything else and establishes no inventory. Placement refuses it, which is right: sending a Run pinned to eight cards to a machine nobody counted is a launch nobody can promise. What the refusal says is the point. A machine nobody counted is not a machine with no cards, so the wait names the silence and the fleet's answer counts the machine as one that said too little to tell rather than as one that can never run this work. Only a Run that separately declares facts nvidia_driver ever reaches the machine's attestation, and no GPU Run is written that way: a Run states a count, a model, or a memory floor, and read as a measured zero the empty inventory struck an eight-card machine out with RESOURCE_INSUFFICIENT, which is the strongest thing a fleet can say and the one wait other work does not have to respect. The second Run here is the assertion. It arrives later, it is worth no more than the Run that has been waiting, and it is told it waits behind it rather than inheriting a workspace whose ordering one missing nvidia-smi threw away.
